fsevents watcher implementation:

```js
import { EventEmitter } from 'node:events'
import { loadFsevents } from './load-fsevents.js'

export class FSEventsWatcher extends EventEmitter {
  constructor(paths, options = {}) {
    super()
    this.paths = Array.isArray(paths) ? paths : [paths]
    this.options = options
    this.stops = []
    this.closed = false
    this._fsevents = null
  }

  async start() {
    const fsevents = await loadFsevents()
    if (!fsevents) {
      throw new Error('native fsevents module is not available')
    }
    this._fsevents = fsevents
    for (const p of this.paths) {
      const stop = fsevents.watch(p, (path, flags, id) => this._onEvent(path, flags, id), {
        latency: this.options.latency ?? 0.25,
        since: this.options.since ?? undefined,
        flags: this.options.flags,
      })
      this.stops.push(stop)
    }
    this.emit('ready')
    return this
  }

  _onEvent(path, flags, id) {
    const fsevents = this._fsevents
    const info = fsevents.getInfo(path, flags)
    const event = {
      path,
      id,
      event: info.event,
      type: info.type,
      changes: info.changes,
      flags,
    }
    this.emit('event', event)
    if (info.event && info.event !== 'unknown') this.emit(info.event, event)
    if (info.event === 'root-changed') this.emit('root-changed', event)
  }

  close() {
    if (this.closed) return
    this.closed = true
    for (const stop of this.stops) {
      try { stop() } catch {}
    }
    this.stops = []
    this.emit('close')
  }
}
```

```js
import { EventEmitter } from 'node:events'
import fs from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

export class FallbackWatcher extends EventEmitter {
  constructor(paths, options = {}) {
    super()
    this.paths = Array.isArray(paths) ? paths : [paths]
    this.options = options
    this.watchers = []
    this.closed = false
  }

  async start() {
    for (const p of this.paths) {
      let stat
      try { stat = fs.statSync(p) } catch (err) { this.emit('error', err); continue }
      const recursive = stat.isDirectory() ? this.options.recursive !== false : false
      const watcher = fs.watch(p, { recursive, persistent: true }, (eventType, filename) => {
        const full = filename ? path.join(p, filename.toString()) : p
        const event = eventType === 'rename' ? 'renamed' : 'modified'
        const info = { path: full, event, type: 'unknown', changes: {}, id: -1 }
        this.emit('event', info)
        this.emit(event, info)
      })
      watcher.on('error', (err) => this.emit('error', err))
      this.watchers.push(watcher)
    }
    this.emit('ready')
    return this
  }

  close() {
    if (this.closed) return
    this.closed = true
    for (const w of this.watchers) { try { w.close() } catch {} }
    this.watchers = []
    this.emit('close')
  }
}
```

import { FallbackWatcher } from './fallback-watcher.js'
import { loadFsevents } from './load-fsevents.js'

export async function watch(paths, options = {}) {
  const native = await loadFsevents()
  if (native) return new FSEventsWatcher(paths, options).start()
  if (options.native === true) throw new Error('fsevents unavailable...')
  return new FallbackWatcher(paths, options).start()
}

Project scaffolded at `/work` using macOS FSEvents via the native `fsevents` addon.

- `src/load-fsevents.js` — loads `fsevents` on darwin only
- `src/fsevents-watcher.js` — native backend, normalizes `getInfo()` results and emits `event` + per-type events (`created`/`modified`/`removed`/`renamed`/etc.)

`fsevents` is an `optionalDependency`, so it installs on macOS and is skipped elsewhere (confirmed skipped here on Linux). I verified module loading, the fallback watcher end-to-end, and the `--native` guard. Native code is untested here since this box isn't macOS — run `npm start /some/dir` on a Mac to exercise it.
